label: Colotlán, Jalisco — CJNG Monstruos Border Deployment Apr 18
sub: On Saturday evening, April 18, 2026, a CJNG armed convoy deploying 'Monstruos' (improvised steel-plated armored vehicles) was reported circulating in the Colotlán municipality area near the Jalisco-Zacatecas border. Activity reported across Colotlán, Chimaltitán, Totatitla, Bolaños, Villa Guerrero, and Santa María de los Ángeles; armed clash reported at ~7:20 PM in Laurel, Tepetongo municipality (Zacatecas). No casualties confirmed. Colotlán sits within El Jardinero faction's established northern Jalisco-Zacatecas plaza network — Monstruos deployment is consistent with post-fractura-total buildup positioning. (Borderland Beat, April 19, 2026)

label: Guadalajara — FIFA World Cup 2026 Security Hub
sub: Guadalajara's Akron Stadium is a FIFA World Cup 2026 venue (4 group-stage matches beginning June 15). PLAN KUKULKAN — T-4 DAYS (June 7): 99,000+ security personnel fully deployed at Estadio Akron; anti-drone systems operational. GUADALAJARA VIOLENCE -30% (pre-tournament window vs. prior 5 months) — security analysts. KOREA DAY IN ZAPOPAN (June 6): South Korea's World Cup team held cultural event in CJNG's historic operational heartland — ~16,000 disappearances logged in Jalisco state documented by InSight Crime. CJNG BLACKOUT (Day 105): CJNG operational directive to avoid high-visibility violence remains in effect; post-tournament return to baseline projected. OCCRP (June 2026): CJNG algorithm warfare documented. EL SAPO AT LARGE (Day 105): Pre-June 11 capture objective unmet; World Cup perimeter security now primary focus. 8-NATION TRAVEL WARNINGS maintained for World Cup visitors.

label: Guadalajara — CJNG Headquarters
sub: Metropolitan Guadalajara (including Zapopan) is the historic birthplace and operational center of CJNG. El Mencho built his criminal empire here after the 2010 death of Nacho Coronel eliminated Sinaloa's Jalisco umbrella.

label: Tapalpa — El Mencho Killed
sub: Mountain town in Jalisco where El Mencho (Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes) was killed on February 22, 2026, during a joint Army/GN/Air Force operation with U.S. intelligence support. El Mencho had reportedly used the rugged Sierra de Tapalpa terrain for years as a hideout.

label: Colima — Mexico's Most Violent State
sub: Colima city and state have recorded the highest per-capita homicide rate in Mexico for multiple consecutive years — reaching 111 per 100,000 in 2023. CJNG controls most of the state, including lucrative trafficking routes to the Port of Manzanillo.

label: Port of Manzanillo — Fentanyl Precursor Gateway
sub: Mexico's busiest Pacific port and the primary entry point for fentanyl chemical precursors shipped from China. CJNG controls port security and customs infrastructure, enabling massive precursor imports that fuel fentanyl production for the U.S. market.

label: Port of Lázaro Cárdenas — CJNG-Controlled Hub
sub: Strategic deep-water port in Michoacán controlled by CJNG. Used to import fentanyl precursors, export methamphetamine, and smuggle iron ore with extorted proceeds. The port's strategic importance drives persistent CJNG-Los Viagras conflict in surrounding Tierra Caliente.

label: Aguililla, Michoacán — El Mencho's Birthplace
sub: Rural township where Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes was born and raised. Aguililla became a symbol of Mexican state weakness when Carteles Unidos blockaded access roads in 2020–2021, leaving residents trapped without food or medicine as part of the anti-CJNG campaign.

label: Uruapan — Bridge Massacre Site
sub: In August 2019, CJNG hung nine bodies from a bridge and left 10 more dismembered nearby in this major Michoacán city, as part of its war against Los Viagras for control of Tierra Caliente's avocado and lime extortion rackets.

label: Irapuato, Guanajuato — Drug Rehab Massacre Site
sub: Site of a June 2020 CJNG massacre of 27 people at a drug rehabilitation center — one of the deadliest single attacks in the CJNG-CSRL Guanajuato war. CJNG's campaign transformed Guanajuato into Mexico's deadliest state by absolute homicide count for multiple years.

label: León, Guanajuato — CSRL–CJNG Battleground
sub: Guanajuato's largest city and the arena of intense CJNG versus Santa Rosa de Lima Cartel (CSRL) conflict from 2016 to 2020. CJNG's decisive win in Guanajuato following El Marro's arrest transformed the state into a CJNG-dominated corridor.

label: Villa Purificación — Military Helicopter Shootdown
sub: On May 1, 2015, CJNG gunmen used Russian-made RPG-27 rocket launchers to shoot down a Mexican military Cougar EC725 helicopter near this town, killing 9 soldiers. The attack triggered Operation Jalisco — the largest military mobilization in Jalisco's history.

label: Zapopan — Co-founder El 85 Arrested / El 53 Killed
sub: Guadalajara suburb with a dark CJNG history: co-founder Érick Valencia Salazar 'El 85' was arrested here in March 2012, and co-founder Martín Arzola Ortega 'El 53' was assassinated at a shopping center here on July 31, 2019, by a CJNG hitman.

label: Mexico City — García Harfuch Assassination Attempt
sub: On June 26, 2020, four groups of CJNG gunmen ambushed Mexico City security secretary Omar García Harfuch on Paseo de la Reforma, firing 400+ rounds including .50-caliber. He survived; three others did not. CJNG's ability to strike Mexico's capital signaled extraordinary reach.

label: Tepic, Nayarit — Northern Trafficking Corridor
sub: Capital of Nayarit state and a key node in CJNG's northwestern drug trafficking network. CJNG achieved near-total dominance over Nayarit, maintaining relative stability through hegemony while using the state as a transit corridor toward Sinaloa and Baja California.

label: Zacatecas — CJNG vs. Sinaloa Active Warzone
sub: Zacatecas has become one of Mexico's most contested territories as CJNG and the Sinaloa Cartel fight for control of key highway corridors. Multiple roadblocks, mass killings, and hung bodies mark the ongoing conflict in this formerly calm agricultural state.

label: Boca del Río, Veracruz — CJNG Public Debut
sub: Site of the 'Veracruz Massacre' on September 20, 2011 — 35 alleged Zeta members were dumped on the Boca del Río highway with a narco-banner introducing CJNG (then called 'Matazetas') to Mexico. This was the cartel's first major public announcement.

label: Tepalcatepec, Michoacán — Carteles Unidos Stronghold
sub: Stronghold of the Carteles Unidos coalition and birthplace of the self-defense movement. In May 2021, Carteles Unidos used weaponized drones to attack a CJNG convoy here — one of the first confirmed uses of armed drones by non-state actors in the Americas.

label: Guadalajara Metro — 2015 Narcobloqueos
sub: On May 1, 2015, the same day as the military helicopter shootdown, CJNG simultaneously deployed narcobloqueos (cartel roadblocks with burning buses and armed checkpoints) across 11 Jalisco municipalities to prevent potential military pursuit of El Mencho. Over 100 vehicles were torched.

label: Celaya, Guanajuato — Cartel Violence Hub
sub: Celaya became a symbol of the CJNG–CSRL war in Guanajuato, repeatedly recording some of Mexico's highest municipal homicide rates. CJNG ultimately consolidated control following El Marro's arrest in August 2020, but retaliatory violence continues.

label: Riverside, CA — El Gaucho Arrested
sub: On November 19, 2024, El Mencho's son-in-law Cristian Gutiérrez-Ochoa ('El Gaucho'), who had faked his own death, was arrested in Riverside, California with $2.2 million in CJNG proceeds. His arrest eliminated a key CJNG–U.S. financial conduit.

label: Tierra Caliente, Michoacán — Contested Heartland
sub: The hot lowland region of western Michoacán is the epicenter of CJNG's war with Los Viagras and La Nueva Familia Michoacana. Rich in avocado and lime extortion revenue, the region has seen sieges, clandestine mass graves, and drone warfare since 2019.

label: El Grullo, Jalisco — El Tuli Killed Feb 22
sub: El Mencho's top financial/logistics chief Hugo César Macías Ureña ('El Tuli') was killed by Mexican special forces here on February 22, 2026, in a parallel operation to the El Mencho takedown in Tapalpa. $965,000 USD and 7.2M pesos seized. He had offered 20,000-peso bounties per soldier killed as retaliation incentive.

label: Mexicali, BC — CORRECTED: Mistaken-Identity Arrest Mar 11
sub: CORRECTION (per Aug 5, 2026 DOJ/State reward listing): The person arrested here March 11, 2026 was Ángel Javier 'N,' a Mexicali-based CJNG liaison who shares the nickname 'El Doble R'/'RR' — NOT Ricardo Ruiz Velasco, CJNG's Jalisco-based Grupo Élite commander and the real succession-relevant 'El Doble R,' who was confirmed still at large with a new $10M U.S. reward (alias 'Tripa') as of August 5, 2026.

label: Zapopan — El Mencho Buried March 3
sub: El Mencho's remains were released to his family by FGR on February 28, 2026, and he was buried in a golden casket in Zapopan, Guadalajara on March 3, 2026. CJNG supporters gathered for a low-key ceremony. His burial marks the formal end of his reign as cartel founder.

label: Tlajomulco de Zúñiga — 'El Pepe' Arrested Mar 16
sub: Mexican Army and National Guard arrested 'El Pepe' (José N.) on March 16, 2026 — the CJNG logistics operator who transported El Mencho's romantic partner to the Tapalpa hideout, triggering the surveillance chain that led to the February 22 operation. Key link in the intelligence chain that killed El Mencho.

label: Mexico City — 'Memo' Arrested Mar 17
sub: Juan Carlos Dominguez Jimenez 'Memo,' a high-ranking CJNG lieutenant integral to cartel logistics, finances, and security, was arrested in Mexico City on March 17, 2026. Expected to yield significant intelligence on CJNG's financial network.

label: Tulum, Q. Roo — 4 CJNG Members Arrested Mar 15
sub: Four alleged CJNG members arrested during multi-agency operation in Tulum on March 15, 2026. Firearms, narcotics, radios, and tactical gear seized. CJNG extorts Tulum's tourist economy and uses Q. Roo for money laundering through hotel and restaurant investments.

label: Chavinda, Michoacán — 5 Officials Arrested, CJNG Ties
sub: Five Chavinda municipal officials arrested during Operativo Enjambre on March 19–20, 2026, for alleged CJNG nexos. Seized: tracked vehicle, firearms, narcotics, CJNG insignia, and official government documents. Illustrates CJNG's deep penetration of Michoacán local government structures to protect logistics corridors and the Port of Lázaro Cárdenas revenue chain.

label: Tequila, Jalisco — Mayor Arrested (CJNG Ties)
sub: The municipal president of Tequila, Jalisco was arrested March 29, 2026 in Operativo Enjambre for alleged CJNG nexos — charges include extortion, homicide facilitation, and serving as a CJNG liaison official. Part of a broader pattern of Jalisco municipal government penetration by the cartel.

label: Puerto Vallarta — CJNG Timeshare Fraud Network (OFAC Sanctioned)
sub: On February 19, 2026, OFAC sanctioned Kovay Gardens resort and 5 individuals + 17 companies in a CJNG-linked timeshare fraud network concentrated in Puerto Vallarta. The scheme defrauded ~6,000 Americans of $300 million (2019–2023). This is the sixth OFAC timeshare action against CJNG-linked entities, sanctioning over 90 individuals and entities total. Mexico's UIF simultaneously added CJNG-related subjects to its blocked persons list — reflecting deepening U.S.-Mexico financial intelligence coordination.

label: Rancho Izaguirre — CJNG Extermination Camp
sub: CJNG recruitment, training, and extermination compound in Teuchitlán, Jalisco. First publicly identified in 2025; ongoing forensic investigation in April 2026 found a septic tank with calcined bone fragments predating 2015, nearly 100 DNA samples obtained. FGR: 75% processed, 2 victims formally identified. Scale described as 'much larger than last year.' Represents CJNG's decade-long forced disappearance operations in the Jalisco heartland.

label: Zacatecas-Jalisco Border — CJNG Police HQ Attack Apr 12
sub: In the early hours of April 12, 2026 — coinciding with the Semana Santa security drawdown — a CJNG armed convoy attacked a municipal police headquarters on the Zacatecas-Jalisco border, riddling two patrol vehicles with high-caliber rounds and severely damaging the station. One attacker killed; federal reinforcements requested. Assessed as an El Jardinero faction operation to test post-Semana Santa security response.

label: Coquimatlán, Colima — CJNG Highway Confrontation Apr 17
sub: Three CJNG members identified by Colima State Security Secretary as belonging to 'a previously identified CJNG cell' were killed April 17 during a joint security pursuit on the Colima-Manzanillo highway near Coquimatlán. Forces involved: Municipal Police, SEMAR, National Guard, Army, State Police, State Prosecutor. Occurred one day after eight Manzanillo police were arrested for leaking C5i intelligence to CJNG via Threema.

label: Manzanillo — 8 Police Arrested for CJNG Intel Leaks Apr 16
sub: Eight Manzanillo Municipal Police officers (8–25 years service) arrested April 16, 2026 for using encrypted app Threema to relay real-time C5i system intelligence — checkpoint locations, detention reports, federal force movements — to CJNG operatives at the Port of Manzanillo. Joint SEDENA/SEMAR/Colima State Police operation. Charges: improper use of protected information + criminal association. Mayor: officers 'betrayed citizen trust.'

label: Guerrero — Displacement Crisis: Los Ardillos Drone Attacks (May 16, 2026)
sub: DISPLACEMENT CRISIS (Washington Post, May 16, 2026): Los Ardillos cartel deployed drone-launched explosive devices against indigenous mountain communities in Guerrero — CIPOG-EZ documented 800+ displaced persons, 3 community police killed, livestock slaughtered. Mexico deployed 1,200 security forces. Illustrates post-Mencho cartel fragmentation enabling new violence adjacent to CJNG's Michoacán plazas. Earlier context: A 50-person self-defense group in Guajes de Ayala rearmed in Oct 2025 after La Nueva Familia Michoacana (FTO-designated) resumed expansion into 7 mountain communities. Former CJNG members noted among vigilantes. (AP, March 2026; Washington Post, May 16, 2026)

label: Nicolás Romero, Edomex — Operativo Enjambre: 1,146 Years Sentenced
sub: Origin of the Operativo Enjambre State of Mexico prosecution wave. Discovery of 10 victims' remains in wells here revealed CJNG and La Familia Michoacana infiltration of municipal security forces. On April 25, 2026, FGJEM announced 20 officials sentenced to combined 1,146 years — including ex-Commissioner Adrián Mauricio Sánchez Mitre (190 years) and ex-Mayor Martínez Robles (70 years). Illustrates CJNG's institutional penetration beyond Jalisco-Michoacán into Mexico's most populous state.

label: El Mirador, Nayarit — El Jardinero ARRESTED Apr 27
sub: Audias Flores Silva 'El Jardinero,' CJNG's top regional commander, anti-O3 Fractura Total faction leader, and $5M U.S. bounty target, was captured April 27, 2026, near this community in Nayarit — found hiding in a roadside drainage ditch ~20km north of Puerto Vallarta. Operation: 500+ troops, 6 helicopters, multiple aircraft, 19-month surveillance — no shots fired. César Alejandro 'El Güero Conta' (financial operator) simultaneously arrested in Zapopan. CJNG retaliated with roadblocks and arson in Nayarit; cleared by morning of April 28. U.S. Ambassador praised SEMAR. Garcia Harfuch: 'entirely executed by Mexican authorities.' El Jardinero's capture effectively ends the Fractura Total armed opposition to O3/Los Cuinis.

label: Zapopan — El Güero Conta (Financial Operator) Arrested Apr 27
sub: César Alejandro 'El Güero Conta,' El Jardinero's chief financial operator, was arrested April 27, 2026, in Zapopan, Jalisco, on charges of money laundering and asset acquisition — simultaneous with El Jardinero's capture in Nayarit. The dual arrest eliminates both the operational and financial command structure of the anti-O3 Fractura Total faction in a single coordinated operation.

label: Nayarit — CJNG Retaliation Roadblocks Apr 27–28
sub: Following El Jardinero's arrest, CJNG gunmen deployed roadblocks on Federal Highway 15 at Ahuacatlán, Copales, Ixtlán del Río, and Jala, and on the Tepic-Mazatlán highway at Tecuala and Acaponeta. Six vehicles and six businesses were burned; no deaths or injuries reported. All roadblocks cleared and highways, schools, and businesses restored to normal by the morning of April 28, 2026. Mexico deployed 130,000 security personnel nationwide to deter further retaliatory violence.

label: Tecate, BC — 'El Salo' CJNG Plaza Chief Arrested Apr 17
sub: Salomón Barragán Castañeda ('El Salo,' 35), CJNG's plaza chief for Tecate and surrounding areas, was arrested April 17, 2026 in the Alfonso Garzón neighborhood ('Nido de las Águilas') by Municipal Police, SEDENA, and the FESC (Baja California State Force for Citizen Security). El Salo defected from the Sinaloa Cartel's 'Mayos' faction on December 19, 2025. In four months as CJNG's Tecate plaza chief, he was linked to 80+ forced disappearances (including minors) and 30+ homicides. He operated a surveillance network of 100+ cameras. His arrest illustrates CJNG's post-Mencho territorial expansion via Sinaloa Cartel defectors in the CJNG–Sinaloa war frontlines. (Semanario ZETA, La Voz de la Frontera, April 2026)

label: Manzanillo — 'El Chucky' (CJNG Plaza Boss) Arrested May 9
sub: Lorenzo Sánchez 'El Chucky,' CJNG's plaza boss for Manzanillo and Colima coastal areas, was arrested May 9, 2026 in the exclusive Bahía de Santiago neighborhood of Manzanillo by federal and state forces using aerial drone surveillance. No shots fired. Charges: homicide, kidnapping, extortion, and narcotics distribution. El Chucky controlled CJNG operations at the Port of Manzanillo — Mexico's busiest Pacific port and primary fentanyl precursor entry point. His arrest follows the April 16 arrest of eight Manzanillo police for leaking C5i intelligence to CJNG via Threema, constituting a two-pronged dismantlement of CJNG's Manzanillo port sector. (Borderland Beat, Parriva, La Jornada San Luis — May 9, 2026)

label: Ciudad Acuña, Coahuila — 'El Cabo' (CJNG Recruiter) Arrested May 7
sub: Fernando Daniel Farías de la Cruz ('El Cabo'), CJNG's forced-recruiter for the Rancho Izaguirre / 'La Galera' extermination compound in Teuchitlán, Jalisco, was arrested May 7, 2026 at a property in Ciudad Acuña, Coahuila by the AIC (Agencia de Investigación Criminal). Charges: crimes against health, enforced disappearances, and organized crime/human trafficking. Transferred to CEFERESO Puente Grande, Jalisco. His capture — ~1,100 km from Teuchitlán — illustrates CJNG operatives dispersing across northern Mexico during the post-El Jardinero enforcement surge. Completes the FGR's methodical dismantlement of the Teuchitlán operational chain: El Jardinero (arrested Apr 27) → El Güero Conta (arrested Apr 27) → El Cabo (arrested May 7). (Aristegui Noticias, El Financiero, Infobae México — May 7–8, 2026)

label: Lagos de Moreno — Active CJNG Narcocrematorio Discovered May 17–18
sub: Madres Buscadoras de Jalisco and Madres Buscadoras de Sonora (Ceci Flores) discovered an active CJNG clandestine crematory and training center still burning when found on May 17–18, 2026. At least 16 fosas (burning pits) with calcined bone fragments. Separately, 60 bags of human remains found in El Salto (near GDL airport). Linked to El Cabo (Fernando Farías de la Cruz, arrested May 7, vinculado a proceso May 14) — CJNG's Teuchitlán forced-recruiter — extending the Rancho Izaguirre extermination network into northeastern Jalisco. FGE Jalisco forensic teams conducting peritajes; no official victim count released. (La Jornada, Infobae, Proceso — May 17–19, 2026)

label: El Salto, Jalisco — 60 Bags of Human Remains Found May 18
sub: Search collectives discovered 60 bags containing human remains in El Salto, Jalisco (near Guadalajara's international airport) on May 18, 2026 — simultaneously with the active CJNG crematory find in Lagos de Moreno. The relationship between the two finds is under forensic investigation by FGE Jalisco. El Salto lies approximately 30km southeast of central Guadalajara. (La Jornada, Infobae — May 17–18, 2026)

label: Guadalajara Metro — El Chipo & Jorge N CJNG Financial Operators Arrested May 19
sub: FGR, SSPC, and SEMAR arrested two CJNG financial operators — José Elías Celis Contreras ('El Chipo') and Jorge 'N' — on May 19, 2026 in raids across five properties in the Jardines de Santa Isabel, La Esperanza, and El Salvador neighborhoods of Guadalajara. El Chipo served as financial operator for El Jardinero (arrested April 27) and El Güero Conta (arrested April 27). Charges: crimes against health and violations of the Federal Firearms Law. Seized: firearms, drugs, chemical precursors, packaging machinery, a warehouse of possibly adulterated alcohol, white Ford Raptor and Cadillac Escalade. Completes the third tier of El Jardinero financial chain dismantlement: El Jardinero → El Güero Conta → El Chipo. (Infobae, La Jornada, El Financiero — May 19–21, 2026)

label: Tecomán, Colima — CJNG Ambush & Narcobloqueos May 26
sub: May 25–26, 2026: CJNG gunmen ambushed state police (SSPE) responding to a 911 call in the Caleras community. Multi-agency response (SEMAR, SEDENA, GN, state/federal police) resulted in 2 CJNG killed, 5 arrested (including a U.S. citizen from Atlanta transferred to U.S. custody via Interpol), and 2 police wounded. Seized: 1 artisanal armored truck, AK-47/AR-15/.50-cal Barrett, 7 IEDs, 35 magazines, CJNG vests. CJNG deployed narcobloqueos on the Manzanillo-Colima highway and forced school closures in 4 municipalities — assessed by Colima SSP as 'a desperate measure to protect a commander.' (Infobae, El Universal, El Financiero, Milenio — May 26–27, 2026)

label: Purépecha Plateau, Michoacán — CJNG Colombian Mercenary Offensive (May 2026)
sub: Michoacán's state attorney general (FGE) formally confirmed on May 29, 2026 that 60+ Colombian paramilitary operatives are embedded with CJNG forces conducting an offensive across the Purépecha indigenous highlands. The cell operates in 8–10 pickup trucks and targets the Ciénega de Zacapu / Purépecha Plateau corridor in 10 municipalities: Zamora, Jacona, Tangamandapio, Tangancícuaro, Chilchota, Charapan, Paracho, Cherán, Nahuatzen, and Los Reyes — contesting logging, mineral, and drug transit corridors against the Los Reyes Cartel and Knights Templar remnants. Recent confirmed incidents: May 20 — 3 CJNG killed on Cocucho–Ocumicho road; May 17 — 2 community police killed in Sevina (Nahuatzen). (Borderland Beat, ColombiaOne, Infobae — May 26–29, 2026)

label: Aquila, Michoacán — CJNG Attacks on Nahua Communities May 19–22
sub: CJNG launched three armed attacks against Nahua indigenous communities La Cofradía and Ostula in the municipality of Aquila, Michoacán between May 19–21, 2026. The May 19 assault began at 9:00 AM with a sustained hour-long attack on the community guard post; a second incursion on May 21 at 6:20 AM was also repelled. Community authorities documented 42 homicides and 5 disappearances attributed to CJNG in less than 18 months (7 total attacks). The CNI (National Indigenous Congress) recorded dozens of armed incursions, drone attacks, and explosive devices against civilian infrastructure. Communities demanded federal military deployment. La Jornada: 'Arrecian ataques del CJNG contra comunidades nahuas de Michoacan.' (La Jornada, Infobae — May 21–22, 2026)

label: Puente Grande, Jalisco — 19 CJNG Members Sentenced to 16–18 Years (Aug 10, 2026)
sub: A Jalisco Tribunal de Enjuiciamiento sentenced 19 CJNG members to 16-18 years, 1 month, 22 days for criminal association, firearms stockpiling, and possession of military-exclusive ammunition, stemming from a November 11, 2022 confrontation with SEDENA in Tizapán el Alto (28 rifles, 2,470 cartridges, a grenade launcher, and CJNG-marked ballistic vests seized). The 19 will serve their terms at the Puente Grande federal penitentiary complex, which also holds 'El Cabo' and 'El R-1.' (La Jornada, Infobae, Vanguardia — Aug 10-11, 2026)

label: La Piedad, Michoacán — Army/GN Clash Kills 3 Presumed CJNG, Aug 14
sub: Mexican Army and National Guard clashed with an armed group on the La Piedad–Zamora federal highway near 'Rancho Monteverde,' El Pandillo, on August 14, 2026. Gunmen in two pickup trucks fired assault rifles at the convoy; the exchange extended roughly 2km. Three men were killed and a 16-year-old low-ranking member wearing tactical body armor was found seriously wounded. Authorities recovered 4 rifles, a grenade launcher, tactical vests, magazines, and a gray Renault; prosecutors said cartel-marked items suggest a CJNG cell. (LatinUS, La Jornada, Omnia — Aug 14, 2026)

label: Tanhuato/Ecuandureo, Michoacán — 12 Detained in Raid on Tío Lako CJNG Cell (Aug 19, 2026)
sub: SEDENA-led raid on the 'Tío Lako' (Heraclio Guerrero Martínez) CJNG cell in Tinaja de Vargas and Colesio, municipalities of Tanhuato and Ecuandureo, Michoacán on August 19, 2026. Nine detained, including Tío Lako's daughter and romantic partner, plus 3 subsequent detentions (12 total); 2 properties, 60+ vehicles, heavy weapons, grenade launchers, IEDs, and a drone seized. Triggered retaliatory blockades and vehicle burnings across roughly a dozen Michoacán municipalities. (Diario Las Américas, Univision/N+, Infobae, La Jornada, Excélsior — Aug 19-20, 2026) UPDATE (Aug 21): A confrontation during the raid left a preliminary count of 5 civilians killed, per Infobae; SEDENA has not independently confirmed the toll. Tío Lako himself was not captured; unconfirmed reporting from journalist Luis Chaparro claims he was killed, disputed by federal sources. STILL AT LARGE (Aug 22): La Jornada reports the hunt continuing across Michoacán and Jalisco.

label: Hidalgo — 20 CJNG Detained, Exotic Animals Seized in Multi-State Raid (Aug 24, 2026)
sub: Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch announced August 24, 2026 that federal forces detained 20 alleged CJNG members in coordinated actions carried out August 21-23 across 36 properties spanning Hidalgo, Jalisco, and Michoacán. Seizures included firearms, fentanyl/methamphetamine/marijuana, 113 vehicles, a drone and jammer, plus tigers, panthers, and other animals held in inadequate captivity. Combined with the Aug 19 Tío Lako-cell raid, 32 total CJNG members detained in under a week. Point placed at Hidalgo's state capital as a representative marker for the multi-state operation; exact property locations were not disclosed. (Quadratín México, El Clarinete — Aug 24, 2026)

label: Oaxaca — 'El Abulón,' Los Mezcales/CJNG Second-in-Command, Captured (Aug 21, 2026)
sub: C.M.M.M., alias 'El Abulón,' second-in-command of 'Los Mezcales' — a CJNG-linked armed wing blamed for violence in Colima state — was captured August 21, 2026 in Ejido Guadalupe Victoria, north of Oaxaca de Juárez, in a joint SEMAR/Oaxaca state prosecutor's office (FGEO) operation. (Infobae, La Jornada, Excélsior — Aug 22, 2026)

label: Uruapan, Michoacán — 'El R-2' Named Successor to 'El R-1' Atop Los Rs Cell (Aug 27, 2026)
sub: A Washington, D.C. federal grand jury indicted 'El R-1' (arrested Jul 30) and his brother Rafael Álvarez Ayala ('El R-2'), identified by Mexican authorities as R-1's successor leading the CJNG-affiliated 'Los Rs' cell across Apatzingán, Uruapan, and Morelia, Michoacán. R-2 remains at large. Point placed at Uruapan as a representative marker for the cell's operational area; exact whereabouts undisclosed. (Infobae — Aug 27, 2026)
